results.q: What happens when the output buffer is full while encoding?
answer: This is handled in pb_write() (pb_encode.c:95): it checks `count > 0 && stream->callback != NULL`, and when that is true it checks `stream->bytes_written + count < stream->bytes_written || stream->bytes_written + count > stream->max_size` (line 97); if true it returns through `PB_RETURN_ERROR(stream, "stream full")`; then it checks `!stream->callback(stream, buf, count)` (line 107); if true it returns through `PB_RETURN_ERROR(stream, "io error")`; then it calls one of write_callback(), buf_write() through pb_ostream_s.callback — which one depends on the data at run time (line 107).

buf_write() sets `pb_byte_t *dest = (pb_byte_t*)stream->state` (line 55); then it sets `stream->state = dest + count` (line 56); then it checks `buf != NULL` (line 64); if true it calls memcpy(); then it returns `true` (line 69).

results.q: What happens when the decoder needs more bytes than are left in the input?
answer: This is handled in pb_make_string_substream() (pb_decode.c:393): it checks `substream->bytes_left < size`, and when that is true it returns through `PB_RETURN_ERROR(stream, "parent stream too short")`, so the rest of pb_make_string_substream() is skipped.
pb_make_string_substream()'s caller decode_static_field() checks `!pb_make_string_substream(stream, &substream)` (pb_decode.c:519) and then returns `false`.
pb_make_string_substream()'s caller decode_callback_field() checks `!pb_make_string_substream(stream, &substream)` (pb_decode.c:804) and then returns `false`.
pb_make_string_substream()'s caller pb_decode_ex() checks `!pb_make_string_substream(stream, &substream)` (pb_decode.c:1230) and then returns `false`.
pb_make_string_substream()'s caller pb_dec_submessage() checks `!pb_make_string_substream(stream, &substream)` (pb_decode.c:1649) and then returns `false`.

results.q: What happens when a decoded message is missing a required field?
answer: This is handled in pb_decode_inner() (pb_decode.c:1190): it checks `req_field_count > 0`, and when that is true it checks `req_field_count > PB_MAX_REQUIRED_FIELDS` (PB_MAX_REQUIRED_FIELDS = 64) (line 1194); if true it sets `req_field_count = PB_MAX_REQUIRED_FIELDS`; then it repeats while `i < (req_field_count >> 5)` (line 1198); then it checks `fields_seen.bitfield[i] != allbits` (line 1200); if true it returns through `PB_RETURN_ERROR(stream, "missing required field")`; then it checks `(req_field_count & 31) != 0` (line 1205); then it checks `fields_seen.bitfield[req_field_count >> 5] != (allbits >> (uint_least8_t)(32 - (req_field_count & 31)))` (line 1207); if true it returns through `PB_RETURN_ERROR(stream, "missing required field")`.

results.q: What happens when a varint is too long?
answer: This is handled in pb_dec_varint() (pb_decode.c:1483): it checks `PB_LTYPE(field->type) == PB_LTYPE_UVARINT`, and when that is true it checks `!pb_decode_varint(stream, &value)` (line 1486); if true it returns `false` straight away; then it checks `field->data_size == sizeof(pb_uint64_t)` (line 1490); if true it sets `clamped = *(pb_uint64_t*)field->pData = value`; then it checks `field->data_size == sizeof(uint32_t)` (line 1492); if true it sets `clamped = *(uint32_t*)field->pData = (uint32_t)value`; then it checks `field->data_size == sizeof(uint_least16_t)` (line 1494); if true it sets `clamped = *(uint_least16_t*)field->pData = (uint_least16_t)value`; then it checks `field->data_size == sizeof(uint_least8_t)` (line 1496); if true it sets `clamped = *(uint_least8_t*)field->pData = (uint_least8_t)value`; otherwise it returns through `PB_RETURN_ERROR(stream, "invalid data_size")`; then it checks `clamped != value` (line 1501); if true it returns through `PB_RETURN_ERROR(stream, "integer too large")`.

pb_decode_varint() repeats while `byte & 0x80` (line 239); then it checks `!pb_readbyte(stream, &byte)` (line 241); if true it returns `false` straight away; then it checks `bitpos >= 63 && (byte & 0xFE) != 0` (line 244); if true it returns through `PB_RETURN_ERROR(stream, "varint overflow")`; then it sets `result |= (uint64_t)(byte & 0x7F) << bitpos` (line 247); then it sets `bitpos = (uint_fast8_t)(bitpos + 7)` (line 248); then it sets `*dest = result` (line 251).

results.q: What happens when a field arrives with the wrong wire type?
answer: Invalid data is caught in decode_basic_field() (pb_decode.c:431): it checks `wire_type != PB_WT_VARINT && wire_type != PB_WT_PACKED`, and when that is true it returns through `PB_RETURN_ERROR(stream, "wrong wire type")`, so the rest of decode_basic_field() is skipped.
Because it returns early, these do not happen in this case: pb_dec_bool(), pb_dec_varint(), pb_decode_fixed32(), pb_decode_fixed64() — the previous values stay in place.

Bad input is also rejected in other places: pb_decode_inner() rejects it when `!pb_skip_field(stream, wire_type)` (pb_decode.c:1133); pb_message_set_to_defaults() rejects it when `!decode_field(&defstream, wire_type, iter)` (pb_decode.c:1031).

results.q: What happens when messages are nested too deeply?
answer: This is handled in decode_callback_field() (pb_decode.c:809): it checks `PB_LTYPE(field->type) == PB_LTYPE_SUBMSG_W_CB && field->pSize != NULL`, and when that is true it sets `*(pb_size_t*)field->pSize = field->tag` (line 811); then it sets `callback = (pb_callback_t*)field->pSize - 1` (line 812); then it checks `callback->funcs.decode` (line 814); then it checks `!callback->funcs.decode(&substream, field, &callback->arg)` (line 816); if true it returns `false` straight away; then it calls one of pb_default_field_callback(), read_callback(), write_callback(), buf_read(), buf_write() through anon.decode — which one depends on the data at run time (line 816); then it evaluates `PB_SET_ERROR(stream, substream.errmsg ? substream.errmsg : "submsg callback failed")` (line 817).

When it does not return there, decode_callback_field() goes on to call pb_default_field_callback() with (`&substream`, `NULL`, `field`) (line 826); read_callback() with (`&substream`, `NULL`, `field`) (line 826); write_callback() with (`&substream`, `NULL`, `field`) (line 826); buf_read() with (`&substream`, `NULL`, `field`) (line 826); buf_write() with (`&substream`, `NULL`, `field`) (line 826).

pb_default_field_callback() checks `field->data_size == sizeof(pb_callback_t)` (line 302); if true it sets `pb_callback_t *pCallback = (pb_callback_t*)field->pData`; then it checks `pCallback != NULL` (line 306); then it checks `istream != NULL && pCallback->funcs.decode != NULL` (line 308); if true it calls pb_default_field_callback(), read_callback(), write_callback(), buf_read(), buf_write() and returns `pCallback->funcs.decode(istream, field, &pCallback->arg)` straight away; then it checks `ostream != NULL && pCallback->funcs.encode != NULL` (line 313); if true it calls pb_default_field_callback(), read_callback(), write_callback(), buf_read(), buf_write() and returns `pCallback->funcs.encode(ostream, field, &pCallback->arg)` straight away; then it returns `true` (line 320).

buf_read() sets `const pb_byte_t *source = (const pb_byte_t*)stream->state` (line 70); then it sets `stream->state = (pb_byte_t*)stream->state + count` (line 71); then it checks `buf != NULL` (line 73); if true it calls memcpy(); then it returns `true` (line 78).

results.q: What happens when an array has more items than its maximum size during encoding?
answer: This is handled in pb_decode_inner() (pb_decode.c:1141): it checks `PB_HTYPE(iter.type) == PB_HTYPE_REPEATED && iter.pSize == &iter.array_size`, and when that is true it checks `fixed_count_field != iter.index` (line 1143); if true it sets `fixed_count_field = iter.index`, `fixed_count_total_size = iter.array_size`; then it checks `fixed_count_field != PB_SIZE_MAX && fixed_count_size != fixed_count_total_size` (line 1148); if true it returns through `PB_RETURN_ERROR(stream, "wrong size for fixed count field")`; then it sets `iter.pSize = &fixed_count_size` (line 1159).
When it does not return there, pb_decode_inner() goes on to call decode_field() with (`stream`, `wire_type`, `&iter`) (line 1169).

Consequence: decode_static_field() checks `PB_LTYPE_IS_SUBMSG(field->type) && *(pb_size_t*)field->pSize != field->tag` (pb_decode.c:553); `PB_LTYPE_IS_SUBMSG(field->type) && *(pb_size_t*)field->pSize != field->tag` depends on runtime values, so it may return early, skipping decode_basic_field() and may call memset() and may call pb_field_iter_begin() and may call pb_message_set_to_defaults().

results.q: What happens when the decoder reads a tag of zero?
answer: This is handled in pb_decode_inner() (pb_decode.c:1088): it checks `tag == 0`, and when that is true it checks `flags & PB_DECODE_NULLTERMINATED` (line 1090); if true it leaves the loop (`break`); otherwise it returns through `PB_RETURN_ERROR(stream, "zero tag")`.

When it does not return there, pb_decode_inner() goes on to call pb_field_iter_find() with (`&iter`, `tag`) (line 1101); pb_field_iter_find_extension() with (`&iter`) (line 1106); decode_extension() with (`stream`, `tag`, `wire_type`) (line 1122); pb_skip_field() with (`stream`, `wire_type`) (line 1133); decode_field() with (`stream`, `wire_type`, `&iter`) (line 1169).

It is called by pb_read() at pb_decode.c:93, only when `count == 0` is false, only when `buf == NULL && stream->callback != buf_read` is true, repeatedly inside `while (count > 16)`; pb_read() at pb_decode.c:99, only when `count == 0` is false, only when `buf == NULL && stream->callback != buf_read` is true; pb_skip_varint() at pb_decode.c:261, repeatedly inside `do-while`; pb_skip_string() at pb_decode.c:278, only when `!pb_decode_varint32(stream, &length)` is false, only when `(size_t)length != length` is false. It is also called by pb_skip_field() (pb_decode.c:326), pb_skip_field() (pb_decode.c:328), read_raw_value() (pb_decode.c:354), read_raw_value() (pb_decode.c:361), read_raw_value() (pb_decode.c:365), pb_close_string_substream() (pb_decode.c:410), pb_decode_fixed32() (pb_decode.c:1433), pb_decode_fixed64() (pb_decode.c:1456), pb_dec_bytes() (pb_decode.c:1590), pb_dec_string() (pb_decode.c:1632), pb_dec_fixed_length_bytes() (pb_decode.c:1715). The full chain from the program's start is: main() → listdir() → pb_decode_ex() → pb_close_string_substream() → pb_read().
pb_ostream_s.bytes_written is a field of type `size_t`, defined in pb_encode.h:51 — the code describes it as: "Number of bytes written so far.".

It is set by pb_ostream_from_buffer() (`stream.bytes_written = 0`, line 86); pb_write() (`stream->bytes_written += count`, line 112); pb_encode_submessage() (`substream.bytes_written = 0`, line 768); pb_encode_submessage() (`stream->bytes_written += substream.bytes_written`, line 775).
It is read by main() (line 32), pb_write() (line 97), encode_array() (line 180), pb_get_encoded_size() (line 573), pb_encode_submessage() (line 750).
Following where its value goes: pb_ostream_s.bytes_written → pb_encode_submessage() → pb_write() → write_callback() → send() — so it ultimately influences send(), which is an output (socket send).

In short: pb_ostream_s.bytes_written carries a value produced by pb_encode_submessage(), pb_ostream_from_buffer(), pb_write() and consumed by encode_array(), main(), pb_encode_submessage(), feeding send(). pb_encode_submessage(), pb_write() both reads and updates it, so it also keeps state between calls.

answer: pb_istream_s.errmsg is set by the macro PB_SET_ERROR (pb.h:926: `PB_SET_ERROR(stream, msg) (stream->errmsg = (stream)->errmsg ? (stream)->errmsg : (msg))`), which runs at 51 places in 20 functions, for example pb_read() (`PB_RETURN_ERROR(stream, "end-of-stream")`, pb_decode.c:104), pb_read() (`PB_RETURN_ERROR(stream, "io error")`, pb_decode.c:108), pb_readbyte() (`PB_RETURN_ERROR(stream, "end-of-stream")`, pb_decode.c:127).

pb_ostream_s.errmsg is set by the macro PB_SET_ERROR (pb.h:926: `PB_SET_ERROR(stream, msg) (stream->errmsg = (stream)->errmsg ? (stream)->errmsg : (msg))`), which runs at 18 places in 13 functions, for example pb_write() (`PB_RETURN_ERROR(stream, "stream full")`, pb_encode.c:100), pb_write() (`PB_RETURN_ERROR(stream, "io error")`, pb_encode.c:108), encode_array() (`PB_RETURN_ERROR(stream, "array max size exceeded")`, pb_encode.c:151).

It is written here: `stream->errmsg = substream.errmsg` in pb_encode_submessage() (pb_encode.c:745); `stream->errmsg = substream.errmsg` in pb_encode_submessage() (pb_encode.c:778); `stream->errmsg = NULL` in pb_decode_tag() (pb_decode.c:308); `stream->errmsg = substream->errmsg` in pb_close_string_substream() (pb_decode.c:417); `stream.errmsg = NULL` in pb_ostream_from_buffer() (pb_encode.c:88); `substream.errmsg = NULL` in pb_encode_submessage() (pb_encode.c:770).

There is no `pb_decode_json` in this code (none of its 869 indexed symbols has that name). The closest names are PB_DECODE_NOINIT (pb_decode.h:122), PB_DECODE_DELIMITED (pb_decode.h:123), PB_DECODE_NULLTERMINATED (pb_decode.h:124), described below.
